title: Statistical Methods for Estimating the non-random Content of Financial Markets

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a high-frequency trend-following trading strategy on the Euro future contract (EC) using 5-minute sampling. The strategy incorporates volatility-based sub-triggers and optimizes 8 parameters on an in-sample period (2000-2007) to maximize the Sharpe ratio. It is validated using out-of-sample (2008-2009) and live-sample (2010-2011) periods, alongside extensive stress testing including data randomization and execution delays.
extraction.data_period: January 2000 till August 2011, five minutes sampling

performance_metrics.context: Average Sharpe ratio across all considered stress tests on the in-sample data and its randomized version

key_findings: The non-random content of high-frequency financial time series can be detected using multivariate statistical analysis and hypothesis testing.
A trend-following strategy combined with volatility-based sub-triggers yields profitable results net of transaction costs on the Euro future contract.
The trading system is robust against data randomization and various stress tests (such as execution delays and increased fees), maintaining an average Sharpe ratio of 2.2.
The strategy operates at high frequency with an average trade duration of 25 minutes.
limitations: Specific details of the model parameters and the exact mathematical formulation of the volatility sub-triggers are not provided in this paper.
A global rationale explanation of the trading system's parameters and herding behaviors is complex, not unique, and noted as beyond the scope of the article.
extraction.extraction_notes: The paper does not explicitly report the final out-of-sample or live-sample Sharpe ratios or annualized returns as exact numbers in the text, showing them only in figures. Thus, only the stress-test average Sharpe ratio (2.2), its RMS (0.8), and the average trade duration (25 minutes) are extracted as quantitative metrics.
